issues.detail: The skill is limited to Chrome 149+ and Edge 150 with no documented fallback strategy for Safari, Firefox, and older browser versions.

scenarios.name: notes-app-searchable
scenarios.rationale: Response A directly implements all rubric requirements: registers two search tools with proper inputSchema (keyword and tag parameters), marks both with readOnlyHint: true, and returns structured note objects with id and content fields—plus provides working, tested code. Response B asks clarifying questions instead and provides no implementation, failing every rubric requirement.

scenarios.name: ecommerce-cart-safety
scenarios.rationale: Response B directly implements all three rubric requirements: registers add_to_cart with inputSchema containing sku and quantity, validates input in the execute function, and marks payment tools with consequentialHint: true. Response A provides good security architecture but doesn't deliver the specific tool registration pattern or use consequentialHint, instead asking clarifying questions rather than providing the required implementation.

scenarios.name: cross-origin-product-search
scenarios.rationale: Response A correctly implements WebMCP's browser-based API with document.modelContext feature detection, exposedTo parameter for the partner origin, readOnlyHint annotation, and structured SKU/name/price output; Response B implements a traditional MCP server architecture instead, lacks all browser-API requirements (no feature detection, no exposedTo, no readOnlyHint), and contradicts the 'in their own browser without API calls' requirement by requiring backend server setup.
